title: Scheme presentation criterion for an etale-local morphism property
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], using the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $P$ be an isomorphism-invariant property of scheme morphisms. Etale means [def-weil-etale-morphism]. A property $P$ of scheme morphisms is etale local on source-and-target if (i) precomposing a map having $P$ with an etale map preserves $P$; (ii) etale base change preserves $P$; and (iii) a scheme map $f:X\to Y$ has $P$ if and only if, for every $x\in X$, there are schemes $U,V$, etale maps $a:U\to X$, $b:V\to Y$, a point $u\in U$ with $a(u)=x$, and a map $h:U\to V$ with $fa=bh$ and $P(h)$. Suppose that $P$ is etale local on source-and-target. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. A presentation diagram for $f$ consists of schemes $U,V$, representable etale morphisms $a:U\to X$, $b:V\to Y$, and $h:U\to V$ with $fa=bh$. There exists such a diagram with $a$ surjective. The following conditions are equivalent: (1) $P(h)$ for every presentation diagram; (2) $P(h)$ for one presentation diagram with $a$ surjective. These conditions define $P$ for $f$. When $X$ and $Y$ are schemes, they are equivalent to $P(f)$ in the scheme sense. No surjectivity of $b$ is required in the equivalence.

proof.text: Choose surjective representable etale scheme atlases $c:W\to X$ and $b:V\to Y$ from the definition of algebraic space. Test representability of $b$ on the map $fc:W\to Y$: it gives a scheme $U$ representing $h_W\times_Yh_V$, whose projection $p:U\to W$ is surjective etale. The other projection is a scheme map $h:U\to V$ by Yoneda full faithfulness. Set $a=cp$; the pullback relation gives $fa=bh$. To check $a$ on any scheme $T\to X$, let $A$ represent $h_T\times_Xh_W$. Then $h_T\times_Xh_U$ is represented by $A\times_WU$: on each test scheme its sections are pairs consisting of a lift to $W$ and a compatible lift to $U$, and forgetting the forced $W$ component is inverse to inserting $p(u)$. These bijections commute with restriction. The projection $A\times_WU\to A$ is surjective etale by base change of $p$, and $A\to T$ is surjective etale by the test of $c$. Their composite is surjective etale by the singleton covering-composition lemma. This verifies representability and both properties for $a$ on every test, and proves existence of a presentation with $a$ surjective.

source.place: Tag 02X1 (lemma-lift-morphism-presentations), proof; representable composition expanded on test schemes

proof.text: Fix a presentation $(a:U\to X,b:V\to Y,h)$ with $a$ surjective and $P(h)$, and an arbitrary second presentation $(a\prime:U\prime\to X,b\prime:V\prime\to Y,h\prime)$. Testing the representable maps $a\prime,b\prime$ on $U,V$ gives schemes $D=U\times_XU\prime$ and $T=V\times_YV\prime$. Their projections to $U,V$ are etale. Testing $a,b$ on $U\prime,V\prime$ shows the other projections are etale as well, and $q:D\to U\prime$ is surjective because $a$ is surjective. The two representing schemes for each pullback are canonically identified over both factors: their functors both assign pairs of sections with equal image. Yoneda full faithfulness turns these natural bijections into scheme isomorphisms. The compatible pair $(h\operatorname{pr}_U,h\prime q)$ therefore induces a scheme map $k:D\to T$.

Form the scheme $E=U\times_VT$, with projection $e:E\to T$. This is an etale base change of $h$, since $T\to V$ is etale, so $P(e)$ by hypothesis (ii). The projection $E\to U$ is etale by scheme base change. The relation $h\operatorname{pr}_U=\operatorname{pr}_V k$ defines $d=(\operatorname{pr}_U,k):D\to E$, and $ed=k$. Both $D\to U$ and $E\to U$ are etale, so the cancellation lemma for scheme morphisms etale over a common base makes $d$ etale. Hypothesis (i) now gives $P(k)$. This proves the non-cartesian refinement comparison without assuming $D\to T$ itself etale.

source.place: Tag 03MJ (lemma-local-source-target), first application of Descent Tag 04R1; expanded using descent.tex Tag 04QZ (definition-local-source-target), (i),(ii)

proof.text: For every $u\prime\in U\prime$, choose $z\in D$ over it, using surjectivity of $q$. In the commutative scheme square $h\prime q=\operatorname{pr}_{V\prime} k$, both $q:D\to U\prime$ and $T\to V\prime$ are etale and $P(k)$ holds. These are exactly the witnesses in hypothesis (iii) for $h\prime$ at $u\prime$. Thus $P(h\prime)$. This proves (2) implies (1). Conversely, (1) applied to the presentation constructed in step 1 gives (2). In this argument $b\prime$ and $b$ are used only as representable etale maps; neither is required to be surjective.

source.place: Tag 03MJ (lemma-local-source-target), second application of Descent Tag 04R1; locality expanded by descent.tex Tag 04QZ (3)

proof.text: For the comparison when $X,Y$ are schemes, suppose first $P(f)$. For any presentation square, hypothesis (i) gives $P(fa)$. Form $Z=V\times_YU$ with projections $r:Z\to V$, $t:Z\to U$. Hypothesis (ii) applied to $fa:U\to Y$ and $b:V\to Y$ gives $P(r)$. The map $s=(h,1):U\to Z$ is a section of $t$, and $rs=h$. By scheme base change $t$ is etale; the identity of $U$ is etale (directly from the definition), so cancellation applied to $ts=1$ makes $s$ etale. Hypothesis (i) gives $P(h)$. Hence (1) holds. This uses no surjectivity of either vertical map.

source.place: Tag 04R1 (lemma-local-source-target-characterize), (a) implies (c), via Tag 04R0 (lemma-local-source-target-implies), (4); graph argument written out

proof.text: Conversely assume (2) with $X,Y$ schemes. For every $x\in X$, surjectivity of $a$ gives $u\in U$ with $a(u)=x$. The presentation square, this $u$, and $P(h)$ are witnesses for hypothesis (iii), so $P(f)$. This remains valid for the empty source: the condition at every point is vacuous. Therefore the extended property agrees with the scheme property. The equivalence of (1) and (2) ensures that declaring either of them to mean $P(f)$ for algebraic spaces is independent of the choice of presentation.

The statement matches the source. Hypothesis (iii) is stated as an iff, which adds nothing because the converse holds trivially with identity charts. The source's representable-f clause is out of scope and is not claimed, so nothing is silently weakened. Step 1: the existence argument from the definitional test of b on fc is correct. It shows h_T×_X h_U ≅ A×_W U sectionwise and gets surjective étale from the singleton covering base-change and composition Mathlib leaves. Step 2: D and T come from the definitional tests, q is surjective because a is, and k is well defined since bh·pr_U = fa·pr_U = fa'q = b'h'q. Step 3: E = U×_V T → T is an étale base change of h, so P holds by (ii). d is a U-map between étale U-schemes, so it is étale by cancellation (3) (02GW), and P(k) follows by (i). Step 4: hypothesis (iii) with witnesses D, T, z gives P(h'). Step 5: the graph section s = (h,1) of the étale map t is étale by cancellation, so P(h) = P(r∘s). Step 6: lifting points through the surjective a and applying (iii) gives P(f). Advisory: step 5 implicitly treats a representable étale map between schemes as an étale scheme map; that is the one-line definitional test on the identity. I tested empty X, non-surjective b and identity charts. proof_deps equals the union of the steps' uses. Every cited theorem is a Mathlib leaf, so there are no route or tool_uses issues and no SGA.
